publications.explanation:
Apply the printed test: a strong argument must be important and directly relevant to the decision. Argument I claims that capital punishment is the only way to eliminate the crime, without supporting that absolute claim. Argument II raises a serious possible consequence for victims, which is directly relevant to evaluating the proposed punishment. This explains the paper's keyed choice B, only argument II is strong.

Here “strong” is the exercise's relevance judgement. It does not establish that the predicted consequence will occur or prove an empirical claim about deterrence.

publications.paper_id: Old_Questions/Direct_2023-2025/MCS Combined 2023 Preliminary Exam Paper-I Series 'C'..pdf
publications.explanation:
The recorded official-key answer is A, microwave. Ionization means removing an electron from an atom or molecule. Microwave radiation has insufficient photon energy to do this; beta particles and gamma rays are ionizing forms of radiation. [EPA: Radiation Basics](https://www.epa.gov/radiation/radiation-basics).

The UV option needs a caveat: “UV rays” covers a range of energies. CDC places the ionizing/non-ionizing boundary within the ultraviolet region and identifies UV reaching Earth's surface as non-ionizing. The question therefore leaves the UV wavelength unspecified; do not learn that all UV is ionizing or infer that A is the only scientifically defensible non-ionizing choice from this wording alone. This clarification retains the historical key. [CDC: About Non-Ionizing Radiation](https://www.cdc.gov/radiation-health/about/non-ionizing-radiation.html).

publications.paper_id: Old_Questions/Direct_2023-2025/MCS Combined 2023 Preliminary Exam Paper-I Series 'C'..pdf
publications.explanation:
The paper's recorded official-key answer is D, Autonomous District Council. The distinction is between the Panchayat/Municipality framework and the separate Sixth Schedule arrangements. Part IX provides for Panchayats, while Part IXA provides for Municipalities, including Municipal Councils and Municipal Corporations. Sixth Schedule District Councils administer autonomous districts under a different constitutional framework.

The question's wording is broad: it should not be read as saying that Autonomous District Councils have no self-governing role. Their separate constitutional status explains the contrast intended by the keyed answer; they are not simply another type of Panchayat or Municipality. See Articles 243B and 243Q and Sixth Schedule paragraph 2(4) in the [Constitution of India](https://www.legislative.gov.in/static/uploads/2025/07/359f70a69695affb9d72f8393102bd2e.pdf).
